expectations.text: Hero headline leads with outcome/impact, not project name or 'Redesigning...'
expectations.evidence: H1 reads 'InvenTrack' - the project name, not the outcome. The subtitle mentions the metrics but the primary headline is just the project name, which violates the assertion.

expectations.text: At least 2 key metrics displayed prominently in hero section (45% drop, 90min saved, 340 stores)
expectations.evidence: Three metric cards in hero: 45% stock-out reduction, 90+ minutes time saved, 340+ adoption. Displayed prominently as centered cards.

expectations.text: Uses first-person ownership language ('I led', 'I conducted', 'I designed') not passive voice
expectations.evidence: Language is mostly passive or uses 'I' inconsistently. Examples: 'conducted in-depth research', 'was built as a technical solution' (passive), 'I partnered with 4 engineers' (one instance). Lacks consistent first-person ownership throughout.

expectations.text: Does not explicitly claim 'senior designer' or 'senior level' - lets work speak
expectations.evidence: Role stated as 'Solo Product Designer' without seniority claims. Work scope demonstrates capability implicitly.

expectations.text: Explicitly mentions the product is live/in production and used by real users
expectations.evidence: States 'Status: Live (Oct 2024)' and 'InvenTrack shipped in 8 weeks and has been live since October 2024'. Clear that it's live and in production.

expectations.text: Problem section addresses user pain AND business impact, not just UI issues
expectations.evidence: Problem section covers user pain (2+ hours daily reconciliation, no filtering, context switching), and business/technical impact (errors causing findings, fragmentation issues). Both dimensions addressed.

expectations.text: Research section explains WHY specific methods were chosen, not just listing them
expectations.evidence: Research section lists methods: 'User Interviews (6 interviews)', 'Contextual Inquiry (2 on-site visits)' but doesn't explain WHY these specific methods were chosen. The 'Key Discovery' paragraph provides insight but the research section itself is mostly a list.

expectations.text: Output is valid TypeScript/Next.js component with proper exports
expectations.evidence: 'use client' directive present but this is a client component. File has proper export but mixes client component logic with what should be server component patterns. Not ideal Next.js architecture but technically functional.
Responsive classes throughout: md:grid-cols-2, md:py-24, md:text-5xl, max-w-6xl, responsive grid layouts. Mobile-optimized.

expectations.text: Uses semantic HTML elements (article, section, figure)
expectations.evidence: Root element is a div instead of article. Uses section elements but wraps entire content in a non-semantic div container instead of semantic article wrapper.
